::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[How to know that latexmk picks up my configuration file?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/59599/how-to-know-that-latexmk-picks-up-my-configuration-file), asked by [Andriy Drozdyuk](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/4415/andriy-drozdyuk) on TeX Stack Exchange (2012-06-12; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I've put `.latexmkrc`  file into my working directory, but it doesn't seem to be doing anything. Is there a way to check that latexmk picks up my configuration file?
:::

A `latexmkrc` file is just [perl][1] code, so you can just put a `print` statement in it:


```perl
# .latexmkrc

print("Hello, world!  I'm a .latexmkrc\n");

# rest of .latexmkrc
```

For more about useful assignments to make, see the [documentation](http://texdoc.net/pkg/latexmk).  


  [1]: http://www.perl.org/
